subject: FinSight: multi-region DR commitments and carveout request
messages:
From: Alex Dunham <alex.dunham@finsight.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finsight.com>, SRE Team <sre@finsight.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-region DR commitments — RTO/RPO requirements

Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick responses so far. As part of our procurement and security review I need to lock down specific commitments for multi-region failover. FinSight's compliance team requires:

- RTO <= 15 minutes for service restoration after region-wide outage
- RPO = 0 for inference traffic (no loss of ingested requests)
- Cross-region failover plan and quarterly DR tests documented
- End-to-end 99.99% availability for production endpoints (US region primary)

We understand some of this is aggressive. Please confirm whether Redwood can guarantee these numbers in writing, and if not, what the recommended carveouts and compensatory controls would be (dedicated capacity, warm standby, increased monitoring, etc).

Procurement is on a tight timeline — we'd like a formal answer and draft addendum by end of week. I'm attaching an excerpt of our DR runbook and the compliance checklist for reference.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Infrastructure
FinSight Analytics

Alex —

Got it, thanks for the details and the runbook excerpt. I'm looping in Marcus (serving/runtime) and Marissa (account lead) to scope technical and commercial options. Initial items we'll evaluate:

- Dedicated clusters across two regions (active/active or hot-standby)
- KV cache warmup strategies and prefix caching to minimize RPO exposure
- Failover automation and runbook cadence (quarterly or monthly tests)
- Financial credits and SLA language for RTO/RPO misses

I'll follow up with an internal feasibility note by tomorrow EOD and a draft SLA addendum for your review by Thursday. If you're available, let's set a 30-minute call on Wednesday to align on acceptable tradeoffs.

Best,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Multi-region DR commitments — technical feasibility

Team — internal note on feasibility and recommended approach: 

Short answer: we cannot responsibly promise RTO 15m and RPO=0 for cross-region failover on the hosted, multi-tenant product without dedicated changes. The primary constraints are:

- KV cache and stateful inference contexts: cross-region failover requires rehydration of model KV caches; that process can take minutes depending on session length.
- DNS and TLS handoffs: DNS TTLs, cert propagation, and load balancer reconfiguration introduce non-deterministic delays.
- Cold-starts: if a cold region must spin up new capacity, provisioning + model warmup adds time.

Recommended vendor-side commitments we can offer:
- Dedicated reserved capacity in two regions with warm-standby. With pre-warmed nodes and automated KV replication we can target RTO = 30–45 minutes and RPO <= 1 hour.
- Availability: 99.95% regional (excluding planned maintenance). Cross-region failovers may be excluded from the availability SLA but covered by an RTO/RPO clause and a credit formula.
- DR testing: quarterly table-top and annual live failover; optional monthly live failover for customers on Private or Dedicated plans.
- Monitoring: 1-minute telemetry and a priority incident bridge with 15-minute response for P0 events.

If FinSight needs 15m/0 RPO we should propose Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed KMS, synchronous replication, and a runbook exercise cadence — that has a different cost profile.

I'll attach the latency simulation we ran for a warm-standby configuration to illustrate expected failover windows.

— Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency_sim_report_q1.csv
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunham <alex.dunham@finsight.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: pragmatic SLA and commercial tradeoffs

Alex —

Based on engineering input, here's a practical proposal we can commit to in writing as an SLA addendum (attached):

1) Availability: 99.95% regional availability for production endpoints (measured monthly)
2) RTO: 60 minutes for cross-region failover for hosted Dedicated clusters with warm-standby (we can operationally target ~45m but will warrant 60m in contract)
3) RPO: <= 1 hour for inference requests; we will provide best-effort retries and request-level acknowledgements to reduce perceived loss
4) DR Testing: Quarterly DR runbook exercises; optional monthly live failover for Dedicated/Private customers (additional fee)
5) Remedies: financial credits calculated as percentage of monthly subscription for missed RTO/RPO milestones (formula in addendum)
6) Preconditions: customer must purchase dedicated reserved capacity deployed across two regions and agree to a quarterly maintenance window for failover tests

If FinSight cannot accept 60/1 as written, the engineering team recommends Private deployment with synchronous replication to meet tighter RTOs — that would require a separate procurement path and longer lead time.

Next steps I suggest:
- Quick call (Wed 2:00pm PT) to review the addendum and confirm procurement timeline
- If acceptable, we will produce an SLA_Addendum_draft_v3 with strike-throughs for legal

Let me know whether 2:00pm works or propose another slot.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Attachment: SLA_Addendum_draft_v2.pdf
From: Alex Dunham <alex.dunham@finsight.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finsight.com>, SRE Team <sre@finsight.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: pragmatic SLA and commercial tradeoffs

Stephanie —

Thanks for the rapid assessment and the clear options. A few points from procurement and SRE: 

- Procurement: 60m RTO is a material deviation from our baseline (30m). We can consider 60m if we get stronger compensating controls and a lower financial exposure (larger credits and an initial credit for first live failover miss).
- SRE: RPO 1h is borderline but may be tolerable for non-critical inference flows. For IDS and telemetry pipelines we still need near-zero loss.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will include:
- A one-time service credit if the first scheduled live failover does not meet the RTO
- A clause excluding planned maintenance with at least 48 hours notice
- A narrower availability measurement window (5-minute granularity) for incidents tied to failover events

Also, loop in Redwood Legal for the addendum next iteration. We'll circulate our DR runbook to help scope the tests.

Regards,
Alex

Attachment: FinSight_DR_Runbook_Excerpt.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunham <alex.dunham@finsight.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Final proposed compromise and contracting path forward

Alex —

Appreciate the context and the procurement constraints. After talking with Legal and Engineering we can do the following compromise for FinSight on Dedicated deployment: 

- Target RTO: 45 minutes (contractual warranty of 60 minutes) for dedicated, pre-warmed clusters with warm-standby in a secondary US region
- RPO: <= 1 hour for inference; for critical telemetry pipelines we will set up prioritized replication with sub-5min RPO as an add-on
- One-time failover credit: if the first scheduled live failover (within 90 days of go-live) misses the contractual RTO, Redwood will issue a one-time service credit equal to 25% of that month’s subscription for the affected endpoints
- Planned maintenance: excluded when Redwood provides >=48 hours advance notice; emergency maintenance subject to notification within 2 hours and remediation SLAs
- Measurement: incidents tied to failover will be measured with 1-minute granularity, and credits calculated per the addendum formula (see SLA_Addendum_draft_v3)

We will:
- Publish SLA_Addendum_draft_v3 for legal review today (link below)
- Schedule a joint SRE/engineering tabletop next week to walk FinSight’s runbook and align on test schedule
- Open a HubSpot deal record and a DocuSign envelope for the addendum (links below)

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/FS-2028-0447 (deal), https://www.docusign.com/prepare/FS-2028-0447-sla (docuSign)

If this is acceptable I can route the addendum to your procurement/legal and set up the tabletop.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
